details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1665 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The fallback-summary heredoc must stay unquoted so `_runtime_failure_path_line` is interpolated into the editor summary.
  WHY: Re-quoting the delimiter would write the literal variable name into the summary and break the refusal-specific alert path.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1623-1627 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The refusal short-circuit must still `break` after touching `editor_refused.flag`; otherwise retries continue after a safety refusal.
  WHY: Removing the `break` would waste remaining attempts on a known refusal instead of stopping the loop early.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1305-1316 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The per-attempt prompt file creation can race or hit permission issues when retry attempts run concurrently.
  WHY: The attempt-specific temp file handling is not isolated enough to guarantee distinct, writable files per retry.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1343-1622 | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The refusal-detection regex is too permissive and can false-positive on ordinary English text in the validation and short-circuit checks.
  WHY: Reviewers assigned different confidence levels (5 vs 2); using the highest because the same pattern is reused in multiple places.
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1329-1340,1613-1634,1656-1693 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: A stale `editor_refused.flag` and per-attempt prompt file can survive the refusal path and make later runs look like refusals.
  WHY: The cleanup/break path can leave refusal state behind in `PREVIOUS_REVIEWS_DIR`, so later runs may emit the wrong refusal summary and downstream signal. 
- scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:1699-1708 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The refusal-specific runtime-failure text is duplicated inline instead of being centralized.
  WHY: Duplicating the sentinel text increases maintenance risk if the wording ever changes.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:3986-4017 | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The validator’s literal refusal grep is tightly coupled to the exact string written by `scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh`.
  WHY: Any wording drift in the script would silently break refusal detection and the downstream alert chain.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:1484-1491 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The refusal-specific warning adds a suffix that makes the message harder to match programmatically.
  WHY: Automated consumers that expect the exact literal now need extra parsing to ignore the added text.
- .github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml:1483-1490 | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The validator notice and poller warning can both match the same live log content.
  WHY: The refusal branch checks for the validator notice among all log lines, which risks double-matching on shared text.
- tests/test_review_autofix_editor_noop_cascade_contract.py:31-69 | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [mistralai_mistral-small-2603]
  PROBLEM: The new test constants use one naming style while the test names use another.
  WHY: The inconsistency makes the contract tests harder to read and maintain.
- tests/test_review_autofix_editor_noop_cascade_contract.py:177-341 | 
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new refusal tests call helper functions before those helpers are defined, so importing or running the module can raise `NameError`.
  WHY: Python executes top-to-bottom, so the `if __name__ == "__main__"` block can run before the helper definitions are bound.
- .github/workflows/review_autofix.yml:4009-4020,4069 | 
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The validator can race on the summary write and emit `EDITOR_NOOP_REFUSAL` inconsistently with the actual refusal notice.
  WHY: The `GITHUB_ENV` update happens after the grep-based decision, so partial writes can skew the refusal-aware branch selection.
- probably_unnecessary_but_read_if_stuck.md:20.10.1,550-574 | 
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new docs duplicate the same refusal sentinel text across multiple files instead of centralizing it.
  WHY: Future edits to one copy can silently break the validator, poller, or tests that depend on lockstep text.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
